talking_points.headline: Hang Seng keeps opening HK wealth centres even as Beijing tightens scrutiny of mainland money flowing in
talking_points.context_html: Hang Seng, HSBC's Hong Kong-listed subsidiary, opened its second new wealth centre this year at Hysan Place, betting on continued high-net-worth demand even as Beijing tightens oversight of mainland investors' cross-border capital into Hong Kong wealth products. As a live read on how the wider HSBC group is sequencing wealth infrastructure investment against regulatory risk, this is a useful proxy for how WPB's own Hong Kong build-out should weigh expansion pace against the same scrutiny.
source_links: Hang Seng doubles down on wealth hubs — SCMP

talking_points.headline: Following the IPO run-up we covered on 21 August, Anthropic posts its first operating profit — a vendor-concentration signal, not just a valuation story
talking_points.context_html: Following Anthropic's climb toward a ~$2 trillion IPO valuation covered on 21 August, Anthropic has now posted its first-ever operating profit, with Q2 revenue up 50% sequentially to $11.6bn, while OpenAI's Q2 revenue reached $6.7bn but with widening losses. Anthropic is not a hypothetical vendor for HSBC — Wealth Intelligence and the Project Glasswing cybersecurity work already run on Anthropic models — so a profitable, IPO-bound Anthropic reduces near-term vendor-continuity risk just as that dependency deepens, and is worth tracking as a concentration-risk item rather than pure AI-market colour.
source_links: IPO fever heats up for OpenAI and Anthropic — Motley Fool

talking_points.headline: Yuan and HKD bonds outpace USD issuance as borrowing costs rise — a funding-cost shift with a wealth-flow read-through
talking_points.context_html: Issuers across Hong Kong and mainland China are rotating toward yuan- and HKD-denominated bonds as US borrowing costs climb, continuing a broader move away from dollar funding. For WPB this is a treasury-cost signal worth watching alongside client demand for RMB/HKD-denominated wealth products, and it reinforces the same de-dollarisation backdrop behind Hong Kong and Singapore's ongoing wealth-hub tax competition.
source_links: Yuan, HKD bonds surge on rising US costs — SCMP

Competitor Intelligence.title: Hang Seng Bank doubles down on wealth hubs despite Beijing's tighter investment scrutiny
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Hang Seng Bank opened a new wealth centre at Hysan Place in Causeway Bay, its second such facility this year, even as Beijing tightens scrutiny of mainland Chinese investors' cross-border capital flows into Hong Kong wealth products. The bank says it is continuing to invest in its wealth centre network to capture high-net-worth demand despite the regulatory headwind.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Nomura hires ex-UOB Private Bank veteran Chomplern Ueavivatsakul in Singapore
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Nomura International Wealth Management hired Chomplern Ueavivatsakul, a 16-year private banking veteran of Citigroup, KPMG and UOB, as Executive Director in Singapore. The move is the latest in a run of senior private-banker moves across Singapore this month.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Yuan, Hong Kong dollar bonds surge as issuers seek cheaper funding amid rising US costs
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Issuers are rotating toward yuan- and Hong Kong dollar-denominated bonds as US borrowing costs climb, with bond issuance in both currencies expected to keep growing through the rest of the year. The shift reflects a broader move away from US dollar funding across Hong Kong and mainland China credit markets.

AI & Technology.title: Anthropic posts first operating profit as Q2 revenue hits $11.6bn; OpenAI narrows the gap
AI & Technology.summary: Anthropic recorded its first-ever operating profit as Q2 revenue jumped 50% sequentially to $11.6bn, while OpenAI's Q2 revenue rose 18% sequentially to $6.7bn but with widening losses. Both companies are moving toward IPOs, intensifying comparisons of their underlying financial health.
